page: Amazon Web Services g7e.24xlarge is a high-performance GPU-accelerated server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features an Intel Xeon 8559C x86_64 CPU providing 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs operating at 2.4 GHz, backed by 320 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Hardware acceleration is delivered by four NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPUs providing a combined 384 GB of VRAM. System memory consists of 1024 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 6 GHz, yielding 10.67 GB per core. The server includes 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 400 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluation demonstrates top-tier capability in compute, graphic rendering, and machine learning workloads. The processor achieved a PassMark CPU score of 91,429.15 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 21,470.0. In graphics benchmarks, the system recorded 95,118.0 in Geekbench ray tracing. Language model inference tests yielded top-tier results across model sizes, processing 1,278.65 prompt tokens per second and generating 28.21 tokens per second on a 70B parameter model. Network and memory testing showed 127.37 GB/sec static web serving throughput and 6,648.45 GB/sec cached memory read bandwidth.

The server offers substantial resource density, combining massive memory capacity with enterprise GPU execution and high-speed local NVMe storage. A tradeoff lies in the hardware complexity and specialized compute profile, which requires software capable of leveraging multi-GPU parallelism and Intel AMX instruction sets to maximize qualitative cost efficiency. The instance is suited for large-scale LLM inference, high-fidelity real-time rendering, massive database analytics, deep learning model deployment, and demanding compute workflows.
description: Amazon Web Services g7e.24xlarge is a Nitro-based server engineered for intensive accelerated workloads and memory-heavy compute tasks. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor with 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs at 2.4 GHz, it features 1024 GB of DDR5 memory and 7600 GB of NVMe SSD storage. Acceleration is handled by four NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPUs offering 384 GB of VRAM. High-bandwidth networking reaches 400 Gbps baseline speed. Benchmark results place this instance in the top tier for multi-core CPU execution, ray tracing, static web serving, and large language model inference, achieving 1278.65 prompt tokens per second on a 70B model. The high memory density and dedicated GPU configuration present strong qualitative cost efficiency for resource-intensive artificial intelligence, deep learning, database management, and graphics processing pipelines.
